query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Integrating experimental and simulation datasets into a machine learning–based high-throughput screening tool will enable the rapid identification of refractory HEA compositions that exhibit an optimal balance of intrinsic strength, ductility, and low density.
generation.material_initial_state: A vast compositional space of multi‐principal element refractory high‐entropy alloys with largely unexplored structure–property relationships.
generation.intervention: Implement a data-driven machine learning model trained on both historical experimental results and simulation data to screen and predict optimal alloy compositions.
generation.conditions: Standard alloy processing conditions with compositional ranges typical for refractory HEAs; high-quality, diverse input data spanning multiple elements and processing parameters.
generation.structural_mediator: Predicted microstructural features such as lattice distortion and phase distribution that correlate with improved mechanical properties.
generation.mechanism: The machine learning model detects underlying correlations between composition, processing conditions, and resulting microstructure by rapidly analyzing large datasets, thereby predicting compositions with enhanced strength, ductility, and reduced density.
generation.predicted_outcome: Optimal RHEA compositions predicted by the ML model will display superior intrinsic mechanical properties and lower weight compared to those identified by traditional simulation-based thermo-kinetic methods, with reduced screening time and computational cost.
generation.baseline: Traditional simulation-based methods (e.g., thermo-kinetic analysis and ab initio simulations) that require extensive computational resources and experimental iterations.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the approach is contingent on the availability and quality of integrated experimental and simulation data; its predictive power might diminish in compositional regions with sparse data.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of improvement in screening speed and property prediction accuracy is uncertain until further experimental validations are performed; potential limitations may arise in regions where data is incomplete or biased.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a representative set of candidate RHEA compositions predicted by the ML-driven screening tool and synthesize these alloys under controlled conditions. Compare their measured mechanical properties (tensile strength, ductility, and density) with those of alloys identified using conventional simulation-based methods.
measurements: Tensile strength (e.g., via standard tensile tests)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the majority (>50%) of the ML-predicted alloy compositions do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in intrinsic strength, ductility, and density (beyond the variability of conventional methods) under identical processing conditions, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

The computational software could significantly affect the efficiency of HTC since massive calculations are carried out. In the example of the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system, it takes only a few hours on a desktop computer to finish the HTCs (~ 3 × 10 3 ) within the composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element and finally screen out eight potential alloys. The CALPHAD-based HTCs

The CALPHAD approach [38] – [40] is currently the only method that can be used to obtain multicomponent phase diagrams with enough accuracy for practical applications without the need of the heavy experimental work [41] . This argument has made the CALPHAD method a key building block in the two largest driving forces in materials engineering today—ICME (Integrated computational materials engineering) [42] and MGI (Materials Genome Initiative) [43] . The application of the CALPHAD method requires both the thermodynamic database to provide the Gibbs energies (as a function of pressure, temperature, and composition) for the individual phases and the computational software to calculate the equilibrium state by an energy-minimization procedure. Over the past three decades, the development of consistent multicomponent thermodynamic databases has grown steadily, and several commercial software, such as Pandat TM [44] , Thermo-Calc [45] and FactSage [46] , has become available. decision.trend: Over the past decade, research on refractory high‐entropy alloys transitioned from trial‐and‐error experimental synthesis (e.g., vacuum induction melting, mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, selective laser melting) to more sophisticated simulation‐based and thermo‐kinetic studies. Early studies (such as PMC5978046 and PMC7513042) focused on processing routes and phase formation in specific compositions, while later works (PMC6427779, PMC11206460, and PMC10213035) advanced the understanding of processing–microstructure–property relationships in refractory HEAs. However, despite these advances, the vast compositional space inherent to HEAs means that iterative experimental or simulation approaches remain too slow to rapidly identify optimal compositions with the desired combination of strength, ductility, and low weight.
decision.unsolved: A rapid and predictive method to screen the enormous compositional space of refractory HEAs—where intrinsic strength, ductility, and low density must co-exist—remains lacking. While simulation-based approaches have provided insight, they do not yet offer a fast, reliable route to pinpoint the optimal alloy composition.
decision.lever: Implementing a machine learning–driven high‐throughput screening tool that integrates existing experimental and simulation data to predict composition–structure–property relationships for refractory HEAs.
decision.why: Machine learning models can assimilate the wealth of data accumulated over previous studies to rapidly navigate the vast multi‐principal element space. This approach builds naturally on the trend from experiment and simulation towards data-driven inference, directly addressing the need for a rapid, reliable method to identify compositions that achieve the targeted properties.
